units.translation: The Titans are certain daemons cast down from heaven into Tartarus, about whom see Thes. vol. 7 p. 2235.
I saw the Titan god Atlas, subdued in toils and adamantine bonds, in his torments.
I could not persuade the Titans, children of Uranus and Earth.
Another Titaness, Phoebe, daughter of Earth, was seated.
The same below: τιήνη [queen]: the queen, and τίταξ [ruler]: honored or lord, but others say king.

The avenger of blood is fixed.

where it is used in the sense of sexual intercourse, as θρώσκειν [to leap, to mount] and περαίνειν [to penetrate] are used: with which G. H. Roscher in Fleckeisen's Annals vol. 109 (a. 1874) p. 38 compared the gloss of Hesychius τρώζειν: ψιθυρίζειν, συνουσιάζειν [to whisper, to have intercourse], to which should be added Zonaras p. 1753 τρωέζειν (corruptly for τρώζειν): συνουσιάζειν [to have intercourse]. In the former sense ψιθυρίζειν [to whisper] the verb τρύζειν [to coo, to murmur] is used: who uses the present τρώζειν [to whisper] we do not know. Concerning the Aeschylean aorist τρώσαι [to wound], which others also used, although not in the sexual sense, the conjectures of the critics χρῶσαι, πλῆσαι, στρώσαι are vain.

From this unused present form are derived the perfect τέτληκα [I have endured] and, which alone Aeschylus used, the second aorist ἔτλην [I endured] and the middle future form τλήσομαι [I will endure]: about which see Thes. vol. 7 p. 2249.

Thus Wellauer and Ahrensius on the Doric dialect p. 313, after Pauw, who had written μή τι τλῆς τὴν [do not endure her]. In M is μήτι τἀαϊσταν, and in the margin οἶμαι μή τι τλαίης τὰν ἱκέτιν [I think you would not endure the suppliant], which is the conjecture of the corrector.
